labels.note: Jayant answers the questions about killing ENA-to-ENA deals in Sitara with the list of 66 physical deals zeroed out, which is the deal-list step of killing or moving deals between books.
Elizabeth asks Daren to help resolve price differences between Sitara and the customer on two Duke day deals, a deal-price dispute that settlement resolution covers.
Mark tells Daren that El Paso cut Exxon's gas into Oasis by 484 on 6/8/00 and that Oasis kept the delivery whole, a pipeline supply cut passed on for information.
Craig asks logistics to change Imperial Sugar's May nomination to its lower expected volume and raises how to price the buyback, so the core work is a nomination change.

James tells the people who fill in the OPM Hours Survey that the next survey moves to Microsoft Access and asks them to request Access before it goes out, which is part of collecting the hours survey.
Fred answers Daren's request with the Big Cowboy production volumes for October 2000 by meter, which the taxonomy places under production month volumes at a wellhead meter.

Mary forwards the thread assigning Cannon's trades to Kinder Morgan under a new deal and asks Daren whether she should change the counterparty on the sale, which is replacing a deal so the gas has a valid deal.
A system confirmation that Stacey is enrolled in a training class and that the cost centre will be charged $300, unrelated to the listed work.

Kim confirms the Exxon gas purchase contract has evergreen language and that a termination letter is being faxed, supplier contract work no key covers because the contract key is limited to transport contracts and OBAs.
Stella reports 7,394 MMBtu of measured flow at meter 986782 for 8/98 with no matching deal in OSS and asks Daren whether a deal exists, an unexplained flow at a meter.
Lee tells the team he entered Mobil Beaumont's estimated daily takes for late January and February into Sitara, which is receiving and entering a customer's requested volumes.
Howard sends the schedulers the Unify pathing to use for Cilco storage withdrawals and for HPLC transport into and out of Bammel storage, which is how nominated storage gas gets scheduled.
Mary forwards outside counsel's review of FERC orders on seasonal rates for the BPA rate case, which is regulatory review and comment work.
HR tells a large list how to collect new UBS Warburg building access cards, a mass announcement unrelated to the listed work.
A company-wide announcement that Ken Lay has resigned from the board, unrelated to the listed work.
A relative forwards an MP3 attachment to Darron's work address, which is personal mail.
A Great River Energy fuel buyer says he bought three fixed-forward contracts at Ventura from another trader and wants to buy more, a customer price quote and sale that no key covers.
Sheri forwards a joke MP3 about Enron to colleagues and friends, a social note.
Darron forwards the 3/8/01 credit report to Carole Frank without comment, so it carries the credit report distribution.
Darron forwards without comment the list of Aquila and Engage Canada deals to be flipped to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book, a transfer of deals between books.
Darron replies to the auditors' monthly request for natural gas P&L top pages by region that he is travelling and can supply them on Thursday, a step in providing and explaining desk P&L.
Darron returns the analyst needs assessment form to recruiting and points them to the Chicago office's similar need, which is hiring work no key covers.
Darron explains to the curve validation reviewer why the NGI-MALIN, NGI-PGE CG and CIG WIC curves shifted in March, which is review of the price curves used to value positions.
Darron forwards the official post ID list to Jason Wolfe without comment, circulating a post ID list.
Darron forwards a family chain letter to his home address, which is personal mail.
Darron forwards an airline joke to friends and colleagues, which is personal mail.
A general announcement inviting staff to an online talk with the head of ETS Engineering and Construction, a mass announcement unrelated to the listed work.
Engineering tells Michelle that making the TW and Lone Star Ward County interconnect bi-directional would cost about $8,000 to $10,000, a cost input to a commercial interconnect project.
Kevin asks for analysis of how far TW can discount fuel charges for Sun Devil expansion shippers, setting negotiation parameters as part of the project's commercial strategy.
Lynn invites the TW team to a meeting on TW imbalances, which arranges imbalance resolution work.
Michelle sends a joke about Enron to an outside personal address, which is personal mail.
Michelle completes Richard's request for the November to February Mojave (El Paso Topock) index prices, which most likely feed index-priced billing, so settlement resolution is the closest fit.
Michelle forwards BRTI's agreed increase in the daily quantity of transport contract 27748 with the single word Approved, which is approval of a transportation contract change.
An empty message carrying only a local link to a clock web page, with no business content.
Michelle accepts a colleague's dinner invitation, a social note.
Michelle asks colleagues to review the Transwestern available firm capacity posting before Tuesday, which is part of posting available capacity.
Michelle forwards without comment an ETS-wide notice of a floor meeting on the Dynegy settlement, a mass announcement unrelated to the listed work.
Michelle confirms that Williams agreed the cash payment for its cumulative imbalance on contract 21823, which is agreeing how an imbalance is cleared.
Michelle sends Bert a copy of the Western Gas sales confirmation with no other text, which is trade confirmation work no key covers.
CAISO tells market participants that the PDCI transfer capability has been derated and when adjusted schedules can be submitted, a transmission derate affecting schedules.
Tim replies that the EST accounts should stay active until the estate has an alternative plan, a decision on disabling user accounts.
CAISO notifies participants of the 2002 Grid Management Charge rates following FERC's order, an ISO market notice.
Bill forwards without comment Kit Blair's summary of CAISO's proposed 2002 Grid Management Charge increases, circulating an ISO rate proposal.
Bill postpones his group's meeting and passes on the instruction to enter new deals under the EPMI-WEST-PERFORMANCE desk, which tells traders which book is ready for deals.
Bill gives his group the new shared login for the Friedwire website, which grants the team access to an information service.
Bill returns the revised 2002 expense budget for the real-time trading group, which is his part of the yearly plan.
Bill answers that he reaches Stack Manager through Terminal Server, part of confirming traders are set up to trade.
Bill approves the loadshape wording for new hourly West Power products on EnronOnline, which is product set-up work no key covers.

Bill asks Kate to make sure a real-time purchase made after a Palo Verde cut is recorded in the Volume Management flash and to get John Anderson access to the desk's systems, two separate pieces of work.
Bill thanks Alan for the update on seeking FERC clarification of a retroactive CAISO price cap, a step in reviewing a market rule with the regulator.
Bill tells Heather that Chris agreed to an $18,750 annuity from ST-CALI to ST-WHOURLY, which moves profit between two desk books.
Bill names MPC and EPE as the key real-time customers to win back once a new company forms, which is customer strategy planning.
